title: Open-source AI coding tools to evaluate
summary: A conditional shortlist based on project license evidence, model boundaries and channel-specific lifecycle signals.

facts.value: The public repository identifies an Apache-2.0 license.

facts.value: The public repository identifies an Apache-2.0 license.

facts.label: Continue upstream lifecycle
facts.value: Continue's official site says it was acquired by Cursor and its open-source code remains available as a foundation. The repository README says the repository is read-only and describes a final 2.0.0 release; GitHub Releases lists a v2.1.0-vscode pre-release published 2026-06-19, and npm lists @continuedev/cli 1.5.47 as latest, published 2026-06-18. JetBrains Marketplace calls the plugin community-maintained and says CLI development is active. These channel/version claims do not establish current CLI maintenance or a package-specific support commitment.

sections.heading: Treat the shortlist as due diligence
paragraphs: Aider's repository documents terminal pair programming and Git integration. Cline's repository describes an SDK, IDE extension and CLI. These are workflow candidates, not benchmark winners; test the same small repository task and review the resulting changes.

sections.heading: Separate code license from the model stack
paragraphs: A project license does not license a model's weights, a hosted provider, an extension marketplace or the code and prompts sent to those services. Check every layer against the intended commercial and privacy requirements.

sections.heading: Handle Continue as a lifecycle exception
paragraphs: Continue's official site confirms acquisition by Cursor and continued availability of the open-source codebase. The README says the repository is read-only and describes a final 2.0.0 release; the Releases page lists a v2.1.0-vscode pre-release from 2026-06-19, npm lists CLI 1.5.47 from 2026-06-18, and JetBrains Marketplace says CLI development is active. These sources narrow the public release record but do not establish current CLI maintenance, package support or security response.

sections.heading: Run a reversible trial
paragraphs: Use a branch, synthetic data and a real acceptance test. Compare review effort, model/provider cost, update cadence and recovery steps. Keep a fallback until the tool and its external model path satisfy the team's requirements.

pros.text: Aider's public source repository identifies the project license as Apache-2.0.
Cline's public repository provides source that can be inspected as part of a tool and license review.
Continue documents CLI session resume and recommends version-controlling YAML configuration while keeping secrets outside committed config.

cons.text: Continue's README calls the repository read-only and 2.0.0 its final release; Releases lists a v2.1.0-vscode pre-release from 2026-06-19, npm lists CLI 1.5.47 from 2026-06-18, and JetBrains Marketplace says CLI development is active. These channel/version claims do not establish current CLI support or security response.
An open client repository license does not by itself establish the terms of a selected model or provider service.
Cline's open-source repository does not establish its configured privacy behavior; later Terms say extension telemetry is on by default, while an older blog says opt-in.

Continue's documented offline IDE setup requires disabling anonymous telemetry and configuring a local model; neither the guide nor its dated Privacy Notice verifies a selected installation's actual settings or data flow.
Continue documents resuming prior CLI history but does not establish cross-device session export or complete IDE/CLI state migration.

faqs.question: What do Continue's published artifacts say about CLI support?
faqs.answer: The official site says Continue was acquired by Cursor and its open-source code remains available. The README says read-only/final 2.0.0; GitHub Releases lists a v2.1.0-vscode pre-release from 2026-06-19, npm lists @continuedev/cli 1.5.47 from 2026-06-18, and JetBrains Marketplace says CLI development is active. These sources do not establish current CLI maintenance or support for a selected package.

faqs.question: Does an Apache-2.0 client license also license model weights or hosted providers?
faqs.answer: No. Aider's repository identifies the client project license and distinguishes model or provider terms; check each external component separately.

faqs.question: Does Cline's open-source client guarantee local-only data handling?
faqs.answer: No. Cline's Privacy Notice distinguishes BYOK traffic sent directly to a model provider from Cline-provided API-key traffic handled by Cline; its Terms also state extension telemetry is on by default, while an older blog says opt-in. Verify the installed build, setting and provider terms.

faqs.question: Can Continue use an offline local-model setup?
faqs.answer: Continue's official guide outlines an offline VS Code path: install its extension, disable Allow Anonymous Telemetry and configure a local model. Its Privacy Notice, last updated 2026-02-05, describes open-source log and analytics collection unless users opt out and excludes processing performed on a customer's behalf; check notice applicability, the selected package and provider terms.

faqs.question: How does Continue describe paid model usage?
faqs.answer: Its Terms describe model-use credit purchases and recurring subscriptions, with applicable Pricing and Payment Terms in a User Account or Service Order. No numeric amount was verified here; confirm any selected model-provider charge separately.

faqs.question: Can Continue CLI history and configuration move to another device?
faqs.answer: The CLI's `cn --resume` or `/resume` commands restore the full history of a previous session. Continue recommends version-controlling `config.yaml`, and the CLI can load a YAML file by path; secrets belong outside committed config. The reviewed docs do not specify cross-device session export/import or complete IDE/CLI state migration. No transfer was tested.

verdict: Aider and Cline are conditional candidates for evaluation based on the linked repository evidence. Continue remains conditional on clarifying its public channel/version history and confirming the selected package's support path; no comparative performance result has been measured.
bestFor: Developers who want to inspect source and license terms while evaluating AI coding workflows
notFor: Teams treating an open-source client license as proof that every model, service or data path is open or offline
migration: Pin the client version and model route; version only reviewable config files and keep secrets outside source control. Confirm whether session history, account settings, local indexes and IDE/CLI state must move. Continue documents CLI session resume, not supported cross-device export or full-state migration; preserve a human-reviewed fallback and recheck license and maintenance before upgrading.
gaps: Confirm the license of the exact installed package and any model or hosted service; repository license evidence alone is insufficient.

Current Continue CLI maintenance and security response remain unresolved: the repository says read-only/final, Marketplace says CLI development is active, GitHub Releases lists a 2026-06-19 v2.1.0-vscode pre-release, and npm lists CLI 1.5.47 published 2026-06-18. Confirm the selected package, publisher, update path and support response.

Continue's 2026-02-05 Privacy Notice does not establish its applicability to the post-acquisition product, selected client settings or processing when acting as a customer's processor; confirm the model-provider route.
No hands-on comparison or model performance test has been performed.
Cline's client settings and model-provider data handling were not inspected.
Continue's Terms describe credits/subscriptions and account/order-specific pricing terms, but exact account or provider charges remain unverified.
Continue documents prior CLI session resume and versioned configuration reuse, but not cross-device session export or full IDE/CLI state migration; no transfer was tested.
